title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Payments
description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community You Will Join: Payments is key for any healthy marketplace, and is just as central to our product at Airbnb. The Payments org at Airbnb is responsible for everything related to settling money in Airbnb’s global marketplace and makes the Payment experience as delightful, magical, intuitive, and easy as possible. At the Payments modeling team, our goal is to empower the mission by introducing intelligences and personalizations that optimize Airbnb’s massive daily transaction volume to best collect payments from guests, distribute payouts to hosts while preventing fraudulent transactions from happening. The Difference You Will Make: As a Senior ML Engineer for Payments, you will be the catalyst that transforms bold AI innovation - LLMpowered workflow, realtime fraud defenses, and hyperpersonalized checkout flows - into production systems that make Airbnb Payment experience feel effortless and secure; you’ll architect and own end-to-end solutions at global scale, partner closely with product, software, and operations teams to turn complex requirements into elegant, latencyfirst services, and set the technical standard for model governance, continuous learning, and engineering excellence that elevates our entire payments ecosystem while shaping the company’s broader AI strategy. A Typical Day: Spearhead LLM agents, realtime anomaly detectors, and other breakthrough solutions that solve real-world problems and create product magic. Collaborate with product, engineering, ops, and data science to spot high leverage opportunities, refine AI/ML requirements, make principled architecture choices, and measure business value with clear, data-driven metrics. Design, train, deploy, and operate large-scale AI applications for both batch and streaming workloads, ensuring low latency, high reliability, and continuous improvement via automated monitoring and retraining loops. Mentor and inspire teammates, fostering a collaborative, experimentation-driven environment where cutting edge research meets production excellence and every engineer is empowered to push AI boundaries at Airbnb. Your Expertise: 5+ years of industry experience in applied AI/ML, inclusive MS or PhD in relevant fields. Strong programming (Python/Java) and data engineering skills. Proven mastery of modern AI/LLM workflows — prompt engineering, fine tuning (LoRA, RLHF), hallucination mitigation, safety guardrails, and rigorous online/offline testing to minimize training/inference drift and ensure reliable outcomes. Handson experience with at least three of the following: PyTorch/TensorFlow , scalable inference stacks, vector search, orchestration/MLOps platforms (Kubeflow, Airflow), largescale data streaming & processing (Spark, Ray, Kafka) Demonstrated success designing, deploying, and monitoring production AI systems - e.g. personalization engines, generative content services - complete with drift/cost/latency monitoring, automated retraining triggers, and cross-functional collaboration that translates ambiguous business needs into measurable AI impact. Prior knowledge of AI/ML Applications in the Payments domain is highly desirable Your Location: This position is US - Remote Eligible. title: Business Operations and Growth Lead, Asia
description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community you will join: The Chief Business Officer (CBO) organization drives Airbnb's growth and expansion around the world, commercializing our new and existing businesses and executing our global strategy in the market. The Global Markets team sits within CBO and makes sure Airbnb is locally relevant everywhere we operate, working with regions to plan and execute growth across supply, demand, and the surfaces our communities use. Asia is one of the largest growth opportunities in that portfolio and one of the most complex regions to run: Japan, Korea, India and Southeast Asia sit at very different stages of maturity, with distinct competitive sets, regulatory contexts and consumer behaviour. Over the past year, the region has built a new operating system and scaled multiple growth levers from single-market pilots to regional programs. That growth has outpaced our capacity to run it: business reporting, program delivery and the cross-functional roadmap currently sit with one person alongside the regional strategy agenda. We are building a dedicated capability to own how Asia operates and how Asia delivers, and we want you at the centre of it. The difference you will make: This role is based in Singapore and requires regular travel across Asia. In this role you report to the Senior Business Operations and Growth Lead, Asia and work closely with country Business Operations and Growth Leads across Japan, Korea, India and Southeast Asia, alongside central teams in growth marketing, product, payments, supply, policy and brand. You own the Asia business reporting and operating cadence, and you lead the delivery of the region's growth levers and its cross-functional roadmap. This is deliberately an ownership role in insights and execution, distinct from the roles around it. Countries own their market plans and outcomes, growth marketing, product and merchandising teams build the platforms, and Strategic Finance and Advanced Analytics own objective tracking and measurement standards. You own the connective tissue between them: the reporting that gives the region one accurate and current picture, the delivery of growth levers into market, the roadmap accountability that keeps cross-functional commitments on track, and the competitive read that tells us where we are gaining and losing. A typical day: Lead the end-to-end operations and delivery of selected regional growth levers including go-to-market, measurement and optimization Own the regional business reporting structure, inputs and cadence regionally and globally Own the regional view of the cross-functional roadmap across supply, product, payments, policy, brand and growth marketing, and drive accountability on delivery through cross-functional collaboration Own the regional competitive view across both guest and host and enable capabilities locally for country teams for local competitors Build AI-enabled automation into the region's reporting, insight delivery and recurring operations that scales team output Synthesize data, trends, guest and host insights, and analysis into actionable recommendations for the regional business Conduct deep dives into operational, programs or functional topics as needed, working with FP&A to assess business performance across areas of strength and weakness Drive entity prioritization and lead entity setup across Asia markets, coordinating with legal, tax, finance and country teams Your expertise: 10+ years in business operations, strategy, consulting or program management, ideally in a marketplace, consumer technology, hospitality or online travel agency (OTA) environment Experience managing programs or operations across multiple countries with varying levels of maturity, and across time zones A proven track record building and running business operating cadences for a distributed organization: reporting, business reviews, and the follow-through that makes commitments land Exceptional cross-functional orchestration in a heavily matrixed organization, creating clarity where ownership is split across product, growth marketing, payments, supply and country teams Strong operating discipline: cross-workstream roadmaps, launch management, business reviews and executive reporting, and crisp written communication that keeps distributed teams description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. The organization is globally distributed with offices in San Francisco, Dublin, Montreal, Seattle, Singapore, Manila, Gurgaon and an extensive partner network serving all regions. The Difference You Will Make: We are looking for a seasoned Forecasting and Demand Planning Analyst on our Community Support (CS) team. This individual is responsible for demand forecasting and long-term planning across multi-channel contact center operations for our Global Operations team. This role ensures the organization has the right resources, at the right time, with the right skills to meet service level objectives while optimizing cost and productivity. A Typical Day: Demand Forecasting & Statistical Modeling Own short-term, mid-term, and long-term demand forecasting across all Global Operations teams and channels (phone, messaging, email, back-office etc.). Design, develop, and maintain statistically robust demand forecasting models using time series and machine learning techniques (e.g., exponential smoothing, ARIMA, regression-based models etc.). Perform trend, seasonality, and variance decomposition; detect structural breaks, outliers, and demand anomalies. Quantify forecast uncertainty through confidence intervals, error distributions, and bias analysis. Perform scenario modeling for peak demand periods, product launches, growth initiatives, and unplanned demand events. Continuously assess model performance using statistical accuracy metrics (MAPE, RMSE, MAE, bias etc). Establish model governance standards, including documentation, validation, back-testing, and post-mortem analysis. Research, prototype, and implement new forecasting and optimization techniques as business needs evolve. Perform scenario planning and sensitivity analysis to quantify trade-offs between service levels, cost, and utilization. Advanced Analytics In partnership with the Analytics and Data Engineering team, design and build scalable planning data pipelines, dashboards, and automate forecasting and capacity models to improve scalability, repeatability, and timeliness. Use SQL and Python to extract, transform, and analyze large-scale operational datasets to monitor forecast accuracy, capacity gaps, utilization, and operational risk. Decision Support & Stakeholder Communication Present forecast assumptions, methodologies, risks, trade-offs, and recommendations in clear, executive-ready formats and act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and participate in demand/capacity planning discussions in cross-functional forums. Align cross-functional stakeholders (Delivery, Product, Finance, HR, and others) to embed planning outputs into execution and operational decision-making. Identify and implement process improvements, automation, and best practices in the demand and capacity planning area to optimize cost while maintaining or improving customer experience and service-level outcomes. Your Expertise: 10+ years of experience in demand forecasting, capacity planning, workforce analytics, or applied analytics. Bachelor’s degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Operations Research, Engineering, Economics, Data Science, or a related quantitative field. Strong foundation in probability, statistics, and optimization. Hands-on experience building and validating forecasting models (time series analysis, exponential smoothing, ARIMA, regression, hypothesis testing) and capacity models (Erlang, queueing theory, service-level and utilization modeling). Strong understanding of contact center metrics (AHT, ASA, service level, shrinkage, occupancy); experience supporting large-scale, multi-site, or global contact center environments preferred. Advanced analytical skills with strong proficiency in Excel, Google Sheets, SQL, Python and data visualization tools such as Tableau. Experience with WFM tools (e.g., NICE, Verint, Aspect) or planning platforms (e.g., Anaplan) preferred. Strong business acumen with the ability to balance cost efficiency and customer experience outcomes. Excellent communication, executive presentation, and stakeholder influence skills; ability to explain complex analytical concepts to non-technical audiences. Proficient quantitative skills and proven ability to interpret and apply data throughout your day-to-day work, emphasizing the importance of data-driven decision-making. Excellent communication and presentation skills and the ability to communicate effectively with clients via phone, email, and in-person, underscoring the importance of strong interpersonal skills. title: NextStay Fellow, Tech Ops & Programs
description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The community you will join: Airbnb's mission is to create a world where people can Belong Anywhere. We're seeking a NextStay Fellow to help pursue that mission as a hands-on Technical Program Manager (TPM) in our engineering organization. The NextStay Fellowship is a launchpad: you'll join with a strong program management foundation and grow into the full scope and ambiguity of the role, supported by experienced TPMs and engineering partners invested in your success. A typical day: Lead execution of a project with a defined scope and approach, turning direction from your manager or senior TPMs into a concrete, realistic plan built around known constraints. Break work into trackable pieces and use input and output metrics to monitor progress, surfacing slippage before it becomes a problem. Lead alignment of the project team and hold contributors accountable to deliverables and milestones, while anticipating the next set of work. Consult team members or leaders to identify risks and mitigation options; track and manage risks you've already identified through to resolution. Communicate the project's vision and success criteria clearly to your project team and stakeholders, and re-evaluate strategy with guidance from leadership on when to pivot versus stay the course. Ask the right questions to surface potential technical gaps, working collaboratively with engineers and applying a working understanding of sound technical principles. Actively participate in cultural and functional excellence activities—such as Connect apprenticeship (curriculum contribution, mentorship), diversity and inclusion programming (Airfinity, Blocking Bias training), or hackathons—and demonstrate Airbnb's core values in everyday interactions. The difference you will make: As a NextStay Fellow you'll own execution of technical programs spanning multiple engineering, product, and operations teams over several quarters — turning objectives set with your manager and senior TPMs into milestones, delivery plans, and team alignment. Working under the guidance of senior TPMs, you'll hold the program accountable to deliverables while managing scope, schedule, and quality trade-offs, re-planning proactively as conditions change and escalating the decisions that carry real business risk. Core manager competencies include: Scope Management – Partners with the team to define boundaries and milestones against program objectives, enabling informed trade-off conversations and preventing scope creep across teams. Schedule Management – Breaks work into sized, sequenced pieces with clear dependencies, builds a schedule with technical partners, and communicates changes as they arise. Quality – Establishes the expected level of quality during planning and treats it as a fixed constraint alongside schedule and scope. Communication – Keeps stakeholders informed early and often, especially when unexpected issues occur. Stakeholder Management – Identifies stakeholders, listens to their concerns, and sets expectations appropriately throughout the project. Risk Identification – Surfaces upstream and downstream dependencies and risks early, analyzing them within the context of the overall plan. Risk Mitigation – Aligns the team on the mitigations that matter most and executes the recommended path with senior TPMs, so the team can respond calmly if a risk materializes. Eligibility Requirements: We are honored to support transitioning service members. To be considered for this fellowship, please ensure you meet the following criteria: You are an active-duty service member currently enrolled in the USSOCOM Warrior Care Program, Career Transition Internship, or a similar program. (Please note: DoD SkillBridge participants are not eligible at this time). You are able to begin your Career Transition Fellowship by November 2026 and complete at least 120 days of the program before your military transition. You are within 180 days of your military transition (separation, ETS, or retirement) at the time of your fellowship starts. You can provide written approval from your chain of command authorizing your participation before final selection. Your expertise: Experience: Typically 2 years of relevant experience, with a BS or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent experience. Most TPMs spend roughly 2.5 to 4 years at this level, with a minimum of one year before progressing, before moving into a role with more ambiguity and scope. Program Management: Able to build a solid, realistic plan based on identified constraints and track progress using input and output metrics. Comfortable managing scope, schedule, and quality trade-offs, and open to on-the-job training and guidance on prioritization early on. Risk Management: Surfaces upstream and downstream dependencies and risks early, aligns the team on how to reduce the impact of the ones that matter most, and drives identified risks through to resolution — partnering with senior TPMs on the recommended path so the team can respond calmly if a risk materializes. Technical Judgment: Comfortable working collaboratively with engineers; asks the right questions to surface technical gaps and applies sound technical judgement to evaluate solutions and tradeoffs. Communication & Leadership: Exchanges information clearly and seeks clarification when needed. Communicates project vision and success criteria effectively to the project team and stakeholders. Strong written and verbal communicator who can answer questions directly related to their project, and manages the project team to deliverables and milestones. Ownership: Takes ownership of programs and drives them forward, exercising sound judgment on when to resolve independently versus when to escalate and partnering with senior TPMs on the decisions that carry real risk. description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. They partner with talented cross-functional team members across engineering, design, operations, data science, and more, leading teams to execute a shared vision. They are incredibly detail-oriented and hands on. The Difference You Will Make: Airbnb has always been about where you stay. Guest Services is about everything that makes a trip more convenient and special once you're there. A private chef cooking dinner in your home. A massage after a day of hiking. A photographer to capture the trip. Groceries waiting when you land, a ride from the airport, your bags stored between checkout and your flight, a car to explore beyond city limits. As Product Manager, Guest Services, you will help build an entirely new business line and a new reason for millions of guests to open Airbnb. This is a rare opportunity to work on a genuine zero-to-one bet inside a company at global scale. The categories are still being defined, the playbook is still being written, and the ceiling is enormous: every trip is a chance to add a service, and every service is a chance to deepen why guests choose Airbnb. You'll partner closely with the teams building the supply side (hosts and partners), along with engineering, design, data science, and operations, to grow new categories from first bookings into thriving marketplaces. A Typical Day: Define the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for how guests discover, book, and enjoy services—from the first impression to the moment the chef arrives or the car is dropped off. Ship and iterate fast. Prototype and partner with engineering and design to build, launch experiments, read the results, and decide what to double down on and what to kill. Live in the data. Define the metrics that matter, like conversion, attach rate, repeat booking, guest satisfaction, and use them to find where guests drop off and where the biggest opportunities are. Obsess over the guest. Talk to guests, read the reviews and support tickets, take the bookings yourself. Bring the real, unfiltered voice of the guest into every prioritization conversation. Balance both sides of the marketplace. Partner with the supply and operations teams building the provider side, so that what's great for guests is also sustainable for the hosts and partners delivering the service. title: Programs Operations Lead, Growth Levers
description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community you will join: The Chief Business Officer (CBO) organization drives Airbnb's growth and expansion around the world — commercializing our new and existing businesses and executing our global strategy in the market. The Global Markets team sits within CBO and makes sure Airbnb is locally relevant everywhere we operate, helping regions plan and execute growth across supply, demand, and the surfaces our communities use. Local growth levers are one of the fastest-growing parts of that toolkit — guest incentives, host-funded promotions, engagement and CRM, country partnerships, and promotional merchandising. Over the past year we've taken these from pilots to scaled programs including incentives, host-funded promotions and promotional-merchandising. That momentum has outpaced our operating model — execution is spread across regional pods, central growth marketing, product, merchandising, and finance, with parallel roadmaps and no single source of truth. We're building a dedicated program management capability to bring it all together, and we want you at the center of it. The difference you will make: This role requires candidates to be in our San Francisco office for 10% of the year (6 weeks a year). As the Program Operations Lead for Growth Levers, you own the operating system that turns our fast-growing portfolio of levers into coordinated, on-time execution. You bring incentives, host-funded promotions, engagement and CRM, partnerships, and merchandising onto one roadmap, one source of truth, and one operating rhythm — so that product, growth marketing, merchandising, finance, and regional and country operations always know what is shipping, who owns it, when, and what it costs. This is deliberately an execution and coordination role, distinct from the business and strategy roles around it. The lever business owners (regional pods and individual lever DRIs) own their outcomes; the growth-levers playbook and country-planning lead defines what each lever is and how countries should deploy it; central growth marketing, product, and merchandising build the platforms. You own the connective tissue between them — the intake, sequencing, operating cadence, budget-to-roadmap translation, launch governance, and institutional knowledge that make the whole portfolio executable at scale and keep it running when individual owners are away. A typical day: Own one cross-lever roadmap and source of truth — consolidating incentives, host-funded promotions, engagement and CRM, partnerships, and merchandising campaigns across all regions into a single plan Build and run the levers operating system — the cadence, launch readiness, and clear RACI across Global Markets, central growth marketing, product, and finance, with resourcing gaps surfaced early Set up the change-intake and sequencing process — a consolidated intake process for new campaign and lever requests, with clear rules for prioritization, approval, and conflict resolution when campaigns overlap (for example, competing merchandising or incentive placements in the same market and week). Translate budget into an executable plan — track committed versus available spend across levers and markets, turn funding decisions into roadmap changes quickly, and give leadership a live view of where the money is going and what it is returning. Be the connective tissue across a fragmented ownership map — regional business operations, growth marketing, partnerships, and the central product and merchandising teams — driving alignment and unblocking decisions so there is one conversation, not many. Turn the levers playbooks and country plans into shipped campaigns — partnering with the playbook and country-planning owners to convert their strategy into standardized templates, coupon and efficiency-reference (ERF) libraries, launch checklists, and repeatable operations that scale across markets. Make performance legible — partner with Advanced Analytics and FP&A on consistent tracking, post-mortems, and readouts that feed the learning agenda (efficiency, incrementality, seasonality, auto-apply, spotlights) and standardize what good looks like across regions. Own the Global Markets reporting cadence — assemble and steer the Weekly Business Review (WBR) with the RDs, drive the weekly leadership report and the monthly country-performance newsletter, coordinate the team staff meeting, and prepare executive and country-deep-dive reviews — so leadership always has one accurate, current picture of the business and the levers. Run the recurring cross-functional roadmap syncs that keep Global Markets aligned — with payments, advanced analytics, growth marketing, merchandising, and international product — turning roadmap changes, guardrails, and escalations into clear decisions and next steps. Hold the operating system together through peak seasons and leadership absences — keeping the levers and the reporting cadence moving over the summer and other periods when business owners are out, so nothing depends on any one person. Your expertise: 12+ years in program management, business operations, or marketing/GTM operations — ideally orchestrating growth, marketing, or commercial programs across multiple markets in a marketplace, e-commerce, or consumer-tech environment. A proven track record establishing a new operating system or central coordination capability from scratch — intake, prioritization, RACI, cadence, and governance — and scaling it across many teams and geographies. Exceptional cross-functional orchestration in a heavily matrixed org — you create clarity where ownership is split across product, growth marketing, merchandising, finance, and regional and country operations, and you are a trusted partner to senior leaders up to the executive level. Strong operating discipline — cross-workstream roadmaps, change-intake and sequencing, conflict resolution, launch management, business reviews and executive reporting, and crisp written communication that keeps distributed teams aligned. Budget-to-execution fluency — comfortable translating multi-million-dollar budget decisions into roadmap and resourcing changes, and reporting spend and return to leadership. Analytical fluency — you partner with analytics and finance on performance, efficiency, and incrementality, set consistent measurement standards, and are comfortable in the numbers (SQL familiarity a plus). Thrives in ambiguity and transition — comfortable operating while ownership models are still forming, with a strong bias to action, ownership, and ruthless prioritization. Desirable: hands-on experience with one or more growth levers — incentives, promotions and coupons, host-funded offers, lifecycle/CRM, merchandising, or partnerships — and experience across international markets and time zones. Fluent written and spoken English; expected in office ~3 days per week. Your Location: This position is US - Remote Eligible. title: Senior Compliance Lead, EMEA
description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Airbnb’s Legal Department is a global team that will require working with diverse international colleagues around the world. The successful candidate will be someone who is adaptable, collaborative and embodies Airbnb’s Core Values. Candidates will be required to approach complex legal issues with a balance for local and global perspectives, while being adaptable to cultural differences and nuances. A genuine and demonstrated interest in Airbnb and a commitment to ethics, integrity and fostering a workplace that emphasizes diversity and belonging is a must. The Community You Will Join: Airbnb is seeking a business-oriented Senior Counsel with deep experience in global privacy laws and regulatory compliance to join our growing legal team. The Difference You Will Make: You will play a critical role within our global privacy and cybersecurity legal team, and work across multiple global teams and regions providing support and advice to Airbnb’s business. You must have excellent judgment in balancing legal risks with business strategy and a proven ability to learn new areas of law and function independently in a demanding fast-paced environment. We’re looking for a highly adaptable and collaborative person who can handle ambiguity and rapidly shifting priorities with flexibility, patience, and poise. A Typical Day: Serves as the primary privacy legal advisor for Payments and Insurance processes and products globally, shaping how privacy legal requirements are embedded into these products and processes, including advising on the privacy implications of payment processing, payouts, financial product features, and fraud prevention systems across all markets, as well as advising on all privacy legal aspects related to Airbnb's Insurance products, including AirCover, Host Protection Insurance, and related coverage programs. Advises on the intersection of privacy law and payments and insurance obligations globally, including PCI-DSS adjacencies, state and national financial privacy laws in the US, and international payment data requirements, as well as on the regulatory intersection of insurance laws and privacy laws across key markets, where insurance regulation introduces specific obligations, working in close coordination with Payments Legal, Payments Compliance, Insurance Legal, and regional Counsels where required. Advises Commercial Legal in negotiating commercial contracts with payment processors and insurance providers. Acts as a key cross-functional influencer with Payments and Insurance Legal and Privacy Management teams to identify and articulate privacy legal risks, requirements, and tradeoffs early in the product lifecycle. Partners closely with the Lead Counsel, Product Privacy, Privacy Managers, Payments and Insurance Legal, compliance teams and regional product privacy counsels to align privacy guidance across geographies, ensuring consistent standards and localized compliance. Monitors and advises on privacy legal and regulatory requirements related to data privacy requirements and supports associated compliance strategies for payments and insurance products and processing, including with respect to U.S. and other global privacy laws. Provides advice and counsel to the Privacy Operations team on the implementation of global privacy compliance requirements related to data governance and data lifecycle management projects. Your Expertise: 8+ years of privacy law experience with depth in financial data privacy, payments, or insurance-adjacent regulatory contexts. Demonstrated experience advising on global payments or financial services data practices in a B2C or platform context. Experience working across legal, compliance, and commercial functions in a matrixed organization. Familiarity with insurance data regulatory requirements and how they intersect with global privacy law across key markets. Airbnb’s various functions embody the company’s innovative spirit, and our fast-moving team is committed to leading as a 21st century company. The Content & Knowledge Management (CKM) team that you would join makes accurate and authoritative information available at scale by creating, editing, and managing metadata and support content—including the public Help Center and internal knowledge bases—used by customers, CS agents, and consuming applications, including AI chatbots. The Difference You Will Make: The Senior Manager, Content & Knowledge Architecture will help establish and evolve the emerging discipline of content engineering—designing, structuring, delivering, and managing content so it’s strategic, scalable, consumable across surfaces, and efficiently adjusted, rather than a collection of one-off articles or chunks—within our organization. In this leadership role, you'll own CKM inputs and influence infrastructure that construct and ingest an information layer, which serves various audiences and product surfaces. You will own decisions that determine how knowledge is created, updated, architected, organized, stored, retrieved, and surfaced. You'll also steer the cross-functional coordination that keeps CKM content aligned with product launches and other business developments or needs. You’ll lead the teams who run taxonomy and ontology, content tooling and AI-focused optimization, as well as content operations planning. You’ll be accountable for how well they perform together: setting direction, clarifying who owns what, and developing the leaders and teams who make it work. We seek someone who sees how systems underneath our content — taxonomy, tooling, authoring processes, information architecture, and operational planning — increasingly determine whether that content reaches the people and machines that need it. You should understand how user-facing content, metadata, measurement and authoring systems, and consuming applications all depend on each other, and you can spot where inconsistency in one area will eventually break something in another. Most importantly, you should view these as a cohesive unit, not several separate functions that happen to share a roof. A Typical Day: Define and champion the evolving discipline of content engineering within CKM, establishing standards for how knowledge is structured, stored, and delivered across surfaces and applications. Own the roadmap for metadata, taxonomy, and information architecture that determines how content is organized, discovered, and reused. Partner with Product and Engineering to define and prioritize tooling investment that improves content quality, efficiency, and innovation. Establish governance frameworks that embed standards and quality checks directly into content creation, review, and publishing workflows. Define the metrics and reporting that give leadership visibility into content health, coverage, and performance, as well as authoring efficiency. Steer cross-functional coordination that keeps CKM content aligned with product launches and other business needs. Lead and develop the managers and senior team members in your group: set clear goals, give candid feedback, and hold each accountable for results. Own talent decisions for the group, including hiring, calibration, promotion, and succession planning, applying clear leveling criteria so people are developed and recognized fairly. title: Senior Manager, Technical Brand & Content
description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community You Will Join: Airbnb’s mission is to create a world where people can Belong Anywhere. As we work to achieve that mission, our cross functional Tech Operations and Programs team helps enable Tech organizations to execute and deliver on high impact programs and initiatives. The Difference You Will Make: You will decide what the engineering world knows about Airbnb. Our engineers solve hard problems at scale across infrastructure, data, and applied AI — and they write about that work well. Almost none of the engineers we'd most like to hire have ever seen it. You'll change that, and the change is measurable. A year in, senior candidates should arrive already able to describe our technical work accurately, because they found it before we found them. Our engineers should be recognised names in their fields rather than anonymous authors. Airbnb should be the source people cite on at least one technical domain. And the strongest engineers in the market should have a reason to choose us that has nothing to do with the offer. That is a rare kind of impact for this discipline. Most tech brand roles are asked to manufacture credibility that isn't there. Here the engineering is genuinely strong and already documented — the gap is that it doesn't travel. You'd be building the function that closes it, with real autonomy, very little inherited process, and direct access to engineering leaders and our CTO. A Typical Day: Own the editorial engine. Run the Airbnb Tech Blog end to end: sourcing topics from teams, coaching engineer-authors, editing to a high bar, and moving posts through legal, security and comms review without letting them stall. Set and hold a publishing rhythm the org can rely on. Find the cross-team narratives. Our biggest gap is that individually strong posts never add up to a story. You'll work across orgs to identify the themes that connect work from multiple teams, and publish them as connected sets — while each domain keeps publishing in depth for its own specialists. Build our voices. Help our engineers and technical leaders develop genuine public presence: bylines, talks, speaker coaching, and a pipeline of new voices. This includes partnering closely with our CTO to establish his public technical presence. Own distribution. Establish our canonical home on an Airbnb-owned domain, stand up the surfaces we're missing including video, and decide what our social channels are for. Publishing well and distributing poorly is the pattern we're here to break. Run our external presence. Set conference and event strategy — where we speak, where we sponsor, where we skip — and manage what we host ourselves. Own our academic collaborations and technical media relationships, and the budget and vendors behind all of it. Steward our open source presence. Make sure what Airbnb claims publicly is accurate and actually maintained, and that the projects carrying our name reflect how we want to be seen. Prove it works. Partner with Talent Acquisition to connect this work to hiring outcomes — inbound share of the senior pipeline, offer acceptance at staff level and above in ML and infrastructure — and be honest about what is and isn't attributable. Your Expertise: Substantial experience in technical content, developer relations, engineering communications or technical editorial — including time spent working directly with engineers, not adjacent to them. Technical fluency. You don't need to write production code, but you need to hold your own in a systems design conversation, read a design doc, and judge whether a draft post says anything real. Credibility with staff engineers is the difference between this role working and not working. Editorial judgment and hands-on craft. You can edit an engineer's draft into something sharper without flattening their voice, and you know the difference between a post that teaches something and one that announces something. Influence without authority. Nothing you need is owned by you. You've built systems and incentives that got busy senior people to produce, rather than relying on persistence. Program discipline. You've owned events, budgets and vendors end to end, and you're comfortable with the unglamorous half of the job. Measurement literacy. You connect brand work to funnel outcomes, and you're straight about the limits of attribution rather than reaching for impressions. Judgment on risk. You've navigated legal and security review, and you know what shouldn't be published as well as what should. Nice to have Experience migrating a technical publication between platforms, including the SEO and redirect work. Experience running or fixing an open source program. Experience helping a senior executive build a public technical presence. Familiarity with AI and ML engineering topics, and with academic or research communications. description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community You Will Join: Airbnb's mission is to create a world where people can Belong Anywhere. As we grow to achieve that mission, we're looking to add a technical, hands-on, and mission-driven Senior Manager of Technical Program Management (TPM) for the Infrastructure TPM team. You will lead a team of TPMs driving multi-org programs across Data Infrastructure, Reliability Engineering, and Developer Experience. Data Infrastructure builds the batch, streaming, and real-time data and feature platforms, semantic metrics layer, and query engines that power analytics, experimentation, and ML, and is making the data stack AI-ready and cost-efficient at scale. Reliability Engineering provides the observability, alerting, incident response, and deployment-safety platforms (progressive delivery and automated rollback) that keep Airbnb highly available and resilient. Developer Experience scales the end-to-end developer workflow, including source control, CI, build, code review, deployment, and cloud development environments, so engineers and AI agents can ship quality software quickly and safely. In this role, you will collaborate closely with data, infrastructure, and product teams across Airbnb to develop holistic solutions that ensure the Airbnb platform is robust, highly available, and transparent in its operations. You will partner closely with senior ICs and engineering directors across Airbnb on processes, strategy, and execution. We are looking for a candidate with a robust technical background who deeply understands the problem space, drives requirements, and leverages their infrastructure engineering expertise to resolve strategic challenges that align with Airbnb’s larger goals. The Difference You Will Make: Our team of TPMs demonstrate ownership, apply skills in whatever combination necessary, and make order out of chaos to achieve the desired outcome. We work hard to ensure teams understand what they have to deliver and by when. We are responsible for aligning teams, identifying or highlighting dependencies, recognizing and resolving ambiguity, setting expectations, anticipating risk, identifying and removing roadblocks, and ensuring the desired business goals are achieved. We are looking for people who share our passion for tackling complexity head-on while building a world class team of Technical Program Managers. A Typical Day: Shape and influence the technical direction of projects, ensuring we meet stakeholder needs while maintaining high-quality standards. Drive phased rollouts and large-scale platform migrations, from pilot through adoption to deprecation, with clear exit criteria and minimal disruption to product teams. Balance broad, outcome-driven thinking with attention to critical details, exercising sound judgment to prioritize where deep focus is necessary to ensure successful execution. Define and secure stakeholder alignment on clear, measurable success criteria, such as availability and SLOs, CI and merge latency, cost per workload, and adoption, and hold programs accountable to them. Regularly assess risks and opportunities, and devise proactive mitigation strategies to maintain momentum and project success. Maintain transparent and effective communication channels to keep stakeholders informed of progress, developments, and challenges. Expertly present outcomes and updates to senior leadership, clearly and comprehensively articulating trade-offs, risks, and emerging opportunities. Hire, develop, and coach a team of senior TPMs, and set operating standards for planning, execution, and portfolio reporting across Infrastructure. Lead programs that prepare infrastructure for AI-driven scale, from CI, source control, and merge systems that absorb higher change volume to agentic developer workflows and AI-ready data platforms. Partner with engineering and finance on infrastructure efficiency programs, including utilization, cost attribution, and workload-normalized cost reduction. Drive cross-org reliability programs such as incident review follow-through, SLO adoption, and deployment-safety rollouts. Own Infrastructure planning rhythms (OKRs, roadmap reviews, dependency mapping) across Data, Reliability, and Developer Experience. Your Expertise: 12+ years in technical program management, software engineering, or SRE, including 5+ years leading and mentoring TPMs or managers of TPMs, creating a culture of inclusiveness and sustainability Demonstrated ability to work through ambiguity to detailed solutions. You can take a vague problem, crisply frame the challenge, identify a path forward, ramp up quickly on new technologies, and drive an initiative over the finish line. Strong technical grounding in at least two of: distributed data systems (Spark, Trino, Flink/Kafka, Iceberg), Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure, observability platforms, or CI/CD, build systems, and monorepos. Track record of leading multi-quarter, multi-team platform migrations or deprecations at scale. Self-motivated, proactive and proven ability to adapt well and work with teams having different operating cadences. Sound business judgment, a proven ability to influence others, strong analytical skills, and a track record of taking ownership, leading data driven analyses, and influencing results Experience delivering infrastructure for AI workloads or AI-assisted engineering, such as feature platforms, LLM gateways, agentic developer tooling, or scaling CI/CD for AI-generated code. Deep familiarity with progressive delivery, canary and automated rollback practices, SLOs and error budgets, and incident management. Excellent written and oral business communication and people skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders. Your Location: This position is US - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a state where Airbnb, Inc. has a registered entity. Click here for the up-to-date list of excluded states. This list is continuously evolving, so please check back with us if the state you live in is on the exclusion list . title: Senior Platform Manager, Data Products, Finance Accounting
description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community You Will Join: Airbnb's Business Technology (Biztech) organization sits at the heart of how we scale our internal operations to match the pace and ambition of our products. Within Biztech, the Finance Accounting Platform team owns the core finance accounting platform — the system that records, processes, and reports the financial lifecycle of every product Airbnb offers to the world. This is a senior finance systems product role: you are the product owner for the platform, its roadmap, and its controls. As a Senior Platform Manager on this team, you will be embedded in a rich, cross-functional community spanning the full breadth of Airbnb's business. You'll partner daily with Product and Platform Managers across Payments, Trust, Guest & Host, Pricing, Insurance, Hotels, and Customer Service — as well as Finance stakeholders from Revenue Controllership, Treasury, Tax, Payments Legal, Consolidation, Collections, and Cash. You'll work closely with Data Engineers and Oracle Applications teams to bring platform solutions to life, and collaborate with FP&A and Business Unit teams who depend on the data your platform produces. This is a role for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance, product, and engineering — often someone who started in accounting or audit and moved into finance systems or a techno-functional product management role — and who finds energy in being the connective tissue across a large, diverse, and highly capable community. Additionally, you bring in that broad perspective and proven track record of implementing platform solutions that scale to changing business needs The Difference You Will Make: You will be the strategic and operational owner of the finance accounting platform — the single point of accountability for shaping how it evolves to support Airbnb's growing portfolio of product offerings. Your impact will be felt across three dimensions: Scaling the platform with Airbnb's ambitions — You will define and drive the long-term roadmap for the finance accounting platform, ensuring it can scale to support new product lines, geographies, and business models. You will own prioritization across a high-volume platform funnel — balancing competing requests with clarity and structured decision-making — and continuously identify opportunities to optimize platform performance and reliability. Bringing new products to life on the accounting platform — Every time Airbnb launches or evolves a product, there is an accounting story that needs to be told accurately and at scale. You will lead that effort end-to-end — from initial accounting impact assessment through solution design, engineering alignment, UAT, release coordination, and production normalization — translating complex product changes into well-designed accounting workflows that record product lifecycle financials to Oracle FAH GL. Comprendre plusieurs points de vue sur un sujet ou une situation. Être en mesure d'évaluer et de présenter plusieurs options pour régler un problème. Être appelé·e, avec l'aide de la direction, à possiblement interagir avec les principales parties prenantes. Execute model optimization within strict millisecond latency budgets at the internet edge, uniquely balancing inference costs against incremental value while maintaining fleet-wide fail-open behaviors. Partner cross-functionally across Engineering, Design, Analytics, Data Science, Finance, Compliance/Legal, Partnerships, and Country teams to execute a shared vision without direct authority. Deep understanding of the payments stack and how money moves in a marketplace environment — across payins, payouts, and the flow of funds. Strong checkout and conversion instincts — a demonstrated ability to reduce friction at the moment of purchase and improve funnel conversion. Hands-on experience with payments fundamentals: authorization and settlement, processors/gateways and acquirers, card-scheme rules, 3DS/SCA, tokenization/vaulting, and reconciliation. Experience with local payment methods and affordability products (e.g., wallets, bank transfers, BNPL/installments). title: Business Development Representative (BDR)
description: About Us At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations Austin, US About the Role In this role, you will contribute to Cloudflare's revenue generation engine by delivering pipeline at scale to the Sales counterparts. You will do this through a maniacal focus on people, process, and tools. The Business Development organization is anchored in a culture focused on the development & training of its employees, incubating talent across the company, teamwork, and celebrating success. With flawless execution, we believe the Business Development organization will be a competitive differentiator for Cloudflare. Responsibilities In this role, your primary responsibility is driving business growth and expanding the customer base of Cloudflare by identifying and nurturing potential opportunities through proactive outreach and effective lead qualification. Prospect and research potential leads or target accounts Initiate outbound calls to introduce Cloudflare products/services Qualify leads based on interest, budget, authority, and fit Build relationships and rapport with potential customers Develop in-depth knowledge of Cloudflare offerings Manage and update CRM with accurate information Collaborate with the sales team to hand off qualified opportunities Meet or exceed set targets and KPIs Stay updated on industry trends and market conditions Provide regular reports and insights to managers and fellow team members Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience Minimum 6 months to 1 year of professional working experience, coupled with an interest in transitioning to a role in outbound sales Minimum 6 months to 1 year of proven experience in a sales or business development role, with a focus on outbound prospecting or lead generation Ability to meet and exceed achievable targets Foundational knowledge of computer networking and “how the internet works” Motivation, drive and a self-starting attitude Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams, such as sales and marketing Experience with CRM systems like Salesforce.com, proficiency in LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and familiarity with tools like Outreach.io or Salesloft would be advantageous Effective communicator with strong follow-up skills Ability to multitask, prioritize, and manage time effectively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment Adaptability, resilience, and the ability to handle rejection or objections in a positive manner Resolute desire to move up in other sales functions at Cloudflare Demonstrated ability to quickly grasp technical concepts and terminology Ability to travel within and outside the United States and/or Canada as required Key metrics for success in this role include: Making a minimum of 50 outbound calls per day Sending a minimum of 30 targeted emails per day using Salesloft Generating a minimum of 2 qualified opportunities per week through calls, email and social outreach Actively managing and progressing sales cadences (Salesloft) Ensuring timely follow-up on all leads or inquiries within 24 hours Meeting or exceeding assigned sales targets and KPIs Keeping CRM data accurate and up-to-date at all times Receiving positive feedback from team members or manager Compensation Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location. The estimated annual salary range includes the on-target incentive compensation that may be attained in this role under the Sales Compensation Plan. Equity This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare’s equity plan. Benefits Cloudflare offers a complete package of benefits and programs to support you and your family. Our benefits programs can help you pay health care expenses, support caregiving, build capital for the future and make life a little easier and fun! The below is a description of our benefits for employees in the United States, and benefits may vary for employees based outside the U.S. Health & Welfare Benefits Medical/Rx Insurance Dental Insurance Vision Insurance Flexible Spending Accounts Commuter Spending Accounts Fertility & Family Forming Benefits On-demand mental health support and Employee Assistance Program Global Travel Medical Insurance Financial Benefits Short and Long Term Disability Insurance Life & Accident Insurance 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan Employee Stock Participation Plan Time Off Flexible paid time off covering vacation and sick leave Leave programs, including parental, pregnancy health, medical, and bereavement leave What Makes Cloudflare Special? We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost. Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states. 1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers. Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you! More details about this will be available at that stage of the interview process. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in. Available Locations: San Francisco, CA About the team The Finance team is a critical pillar of Cloudflare’s success, translating strategy into financial outcomes, and serving as a trusted voice to the public markets, the Board, and our shareholders. The Investor Relations team is a small, high-impact group that tells Cloudflare’s financial story to the public markets — translating one of the most differentiated technology platforms in the world into a clear, credible, and compelling investment narrative. About the role Cloudflare is looking for an Associate, Investor Relations & Strategic Finance to join our lean IR team and help power how we engage with Wall Street. You will be a core contributor to the quarterly earnings cycle, our consensus and financial modeling work, investor events including our annual Investor Day, and strategic finance projects for senior leadership. This is a hands-on, high-visibility role. The work you produce will go directly to the CFO, CEO, Board, and public markets, so we hold ourselves to an exceptionally high bar on accuracy. You will work closely with Finance, Accounting, Legal, Communications, FP&A, and the executive team, and you will get broad exposure to the business and to the public markets. We are AI-native in how we work, and we expect you to treat modern tooling as a force multiplier on insight, productivity, and rigor. What you’ll do Quarterly earnings and consensus Support the end-to-end quarterly earnings process, helping draft and assemble the press release, supplemental financial information, prepared remarks, Q&A prep, and investor deck. Build and maintain our consensus model: collect and analyze sell-side estimates and models, and benchmark them against internal forecasts. Support the guidance process, including share count forecasting, sensitivity analyses, and supporting materials for leadership. Drive tie-out and validation work so that every figure, claim, and disclosure across the press release, supplemental, scripts, Q&A, deck, 10-Q, and 10-K is accurate and consistent. Help prepare for earnings Q&A: anticipated questions, peer transcript research, key stats and proof points, and live-call backup material. Coordinate the post-earnings analyst callback program, including scheduling, notes, and feedback summaries. Investor engagement Support day-to-day engagement with sell-side analysts and institutional investors, including responding to inbound requests and maintaining our investor database. Help plan and run investor events, including sell-side conferences, one-on-ones, on-site investor visits, and non-deal roadshows. Prepare briefing materials for the CEO, CFO, and other executives ahead of investor meetings, including investor profiles, talking points, and Q&A prep. Maintain core IR collateral, including the investor presentation, fact sheets, and IR website content. Analyze shareholder ownership and support investor targeting. Investor Day and strategic finance projects Support the planning and execution of our annual Investor Day, including the invite tracker and registration, content drafting, validation, and day-of logistics. Contribute to strategic finance projects such as peer benchmarking, competitive analyses, long-range financial modeling, and ad-hoc analyses for senior leadership. Analytics and tooling Monitor and synthesize analyst coverage, peer results, investor sentiment, and industry trends into clear, actionable summaries for leadership. Build and maintain the models, dashboards, trackers, and validation tools that let a small team operate at scale. Use AI-native tooling and automation to improve speed, accuracy, and insight across the IR function. Examples of desirable skills, knowledge and experience 3–5 years of experience in investment banking, equity research, investor relations, FP&A, corporate finance, or equity investing; exposure to public technology companies is a plus. Strong financial modeling skills , including building and maintaining operating models, consensus models, and share count and dilution forecasts. Solid understanding of financial statements , public-company reporting, and valuation; familiarity with SaaS or consumption-based revenue models is a plus. Strong written communication skills , with the ability to draft clear, concise materials for senior executives and to turn complex financial or technical concepts into simple narratives. Exceptional attention to detail , and pride in getting every number right. An ownership mindset : you are organized, take initiative, and can manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment, especially during earnings season. High-trust collaboration , with the ability to work effectively with teams across Finance, Accounting, Legal, and Communications. AI-native curiosity and skill : fluency with modern AI tooling and a track record of using it to amplify your impact. Sound judgment with confidential information , including awareness of materiality, fair disclosure, and Reg FD (or a strong willingness to learn). Genuine interest in cybersecurity, cloud infrastructure, developer platforms, or AI, and in the public markets. Compensation Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location. For Bay Area based hires: Estimated annual salary of $117,000 - $161,000 Equity This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare’s equity plan. Benefits Cloudflare offers a complete package of benefits and programs to support you and your family. Our benefits programs can help you pay health care expenses, support caregiving, build capital for the future and make life a little easier and fun! The below is a description of our benefits for employees in the United States, and benefits may vary for employees based outside the U.S. Health & Welfare Benefits Medical/Rx Insurance Dental Insurance Vision Insurance Flexible Spending Accounts Commuter Spending Accounts Fertility & Family Forming Benefits On-demand mental health support and Employee Assistance Program Global Travel Medical Insurance Financial Benefits Short and Long Term Disability Insurance Life & Accident Insurance 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan Employee Stock Participation Plan Time Off Flexible paid time off covering vacation and sick leave Leave programs, including parental, pregnancy health, medical, and bereavement leave What Makes Cloudflare Special? We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet. Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost. Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states. 1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers. Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you! More details about this will be available at that stage of the interview process. Define, scope, success criteria, and technical evaluations plans for Proof of Concepts (PoCs) and Technical Validations. Deliver tailored technical presentations, architectural diagrams, and demonstrations that show how Cloudflare solves specific performance, security, and reliability challenges. Proactively address complex technical objections, security compliance questions, and edge-case architectural requirements during the sales cycle. Take accountability for a suitable solution deployment strategy (Customer, Partner or Cloudflare Professional services) being an integral part of all proposals. Customer Adoption & Value Realization: Provide oversight to technical onboarding and implementation, but not execute the implementation, serving as the primary executive and engineering contact for the customer. Design structured migration and onboarding blueprints tailored to the customer’s environment (e.g. DNS migrations, Zero Trust rollouts, WAF tuning guidance), and act as the lead consultant for customer engineering teams, walking them step-by-step through configuration best practices. Partner with Account Executives to own discovery, demos, onboarding, technical health, risk, and expansion strategy. Proactively monitor customer health scores and telemetry to ensure rapid time-to-value, resolve integration bottlenecks, and reduce deployment risk. Commercial Accountability & Expansion: Carry a variable quota tied directly to new business acquisition and/or ongoing account growth. Be commercially accountable for ensuring deep platform adoption, retaining revenue, and identifying strategic cross-sell and up-sell opportunities based on product usage data. Lead technical Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) to translate platform capabilities into return on investment for C-level executives. Trusted Advisory: Act as a trusted technical advisor throughout the entire customer lifecycle, maintaining a continuous, deep relationship with key stakeholders from initial onboarding through maturity, renewal, and expansion. Provide thought partnership on architecture, AI control layers, security posture, and deployment confidence. Identify potential deployment risks or integration bottlenecks early, and provide remediation strategies to de-risk customer outcomes. AI Orchestration & Workflow Automation: Leverage AI agents, Large Language Models (LLMs), and internal platforms to automate routine tasks such as RFP/Security Questionnaire responses, sandbox provisioning, basic telemetry monitoring, and internal/external documentation, reclaiming your time for strategic customer advisory. Define, document, and educate both internal teams and customers on deliverables such as Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), architectural best practices, and technical guides to continuously raise the technical baseline across the organization. Minimum Qualifications Experience: Experience in a customer-facing technical role, such as Solutions Engineering, Customer Engineering, Professional Services, Sales Engineering, Technical Account Management, or as a Forward Deployed Engineer (years of experience required will vary based on Associate, Senior, Staff, or Principal leveling). Architectural Mindset: Ability to white-board, design, and articulate complex enterprise network and security architectures clearly. Consultative & Advisory Skills: Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate deeply technical concepts into business outcomes for both hands-on engineers and C-level executives. Commercial Mindset: Proven track record of operating in a quota-carrying or revenue-aligned environment, with a strong understanding of SaaS metrics, business value translation, and enterprise sales cycles. Communication: Exceptional presentation and stakeholder management skills, capable of bridging the gap between deep technical implementation details and high-level C-suite business strategy. Technical Breadth: We do not expect every candidate to be an expert in every domain. Performance: Expertise in the performance of Internet properties, including speed, latency, caching, video streaming, HTTP/2, and TLS 1.3. AI Proficiency: Familiarity with prompt engineering, AI-assisted scripting and log analysis, LLM utilization, and workflow automation to augment everyday CE workflows. Coding/Scripting: Proficiency in Python, JavaScript, Bash, Lua, Go, or similar languages to write custom integration scripts, API connectors, and edge computing functions. Developer Platform Fluency: Experience designing, building, deploying or scaling applications using RESTful/GraphQL APIs, SDKs, webhooks, and developer tooling in cloud-native environments. Applied AI Knowledge: Experience with LLM orchestration, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures, and model-access controls. Regulatory Knowledge: Understanding of regulatory requirements such as PCI DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2. Hyperscaler / Digital Native Background: Talent coming out of hyperscalers, digital natives, distributed systems environments, or startups is strongly valued for its deeper cloud fluency and advanced architecture depth. Education Undergraduate or graduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field. In this role, you will develop into an SME across Cloudflare’s products, infrastructure, and controls. What you'll do Security Questionnaires & RFPs: Take ownership of filling out complex customer security questionnaires, RFPs, and technical assessments. Engage with Customers on Security Topics: Act as a trusted security advisor by engaging directly with enterprise customers on security topics. You will meet with customer security teams to resolve deep architectural inquiries, answer specific security questions, and assist legal teams with security terms in contract negotiations. Facilitate Customer Audits: Host, coordinate, and facilitate both on-site and virtual customer audits when customers execute their right to audit, guiding them through our security controls, processes, and compliance evidence. Build with In-House AI Tools: Design, configure, and iterate on custom workflows and compliance assistants using Cloudflare’s internally built AI platforms to automate questionnaire triage and security evidence retrieval. Curate AI-Ready Ground Truth Data: Structure, audit, and maintain authoritative knowledge repositories covering SOC 2, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and global security regulations, ensuring our in-house AI models retrieve verified, up-to-date compliance data. Public Enablement & Trust Portal: Collaborate with marketing and engineering to mature our customer Trust Portal and self-service resources, making it easy for prospects and enterprise customers to evaluate our security posture independently. Author Public Security Content: Research, write, and maintain public-facing white papers, security blogs, and compliance mappings aligned with Cloudflare’s evolving product suite and global regulatory shifts. Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience: 5–10 years of experience in security compliance, GRC, technical audit management, IT risk consulting, or customer-facing security assurance. Demonstrated ability to build with AI: A hands-on builder mindset with proven experience experimenting with, building on, or configuring AI workflows (e.g., prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation concepts, API-based automations, or internal agent configurations) rather than relying solely on packaged third-party software. Control frameworks: Solid understanding of security risk and compliance frameworks such as PCI DSS, ISO 27001, SOC 2, and NIST SP 800-53 Technical writing & translation: Strong written communication skills with the ability to translate complex networking, infrastructure, and cryptographic concepts into clear, plain-language customer responses and white papers. Customer-facing communication: Highly comfortable and articulate when presenting to or answering questions from external customers, sales executives, and legal counsel. Cross-functional leadership: Comfort partnering across Sales, Product, Legal, and internal Platform/AI Engineering teams to drive projects forward. Technical curiosity: Familiarity with data structures, markdown, APIs, or basic scripting (e.g., Python, SQL, or shell) to prototype solutions and inspect model outputs effectively.
